title: Azad or State University? That Is the Question
excerpt: I studied my bachelor's at Azad University and my master's at a state university. Here's my honest comparison, from drama to professors to job market value.

blocks.text: Azad or State University? That is the question!

Well, as someone who did my bachelor's at Azad University and then managed to get into a state university for my master's, and became a top student in both, I'm really in a position to make this comparison. Yes, you read that right! I'm in a position to make this comparison.
Quick Answers

items: 1: Are all state university students great? No
2: Are all Azad University students bad? No
3: Will everyone who studies at a state university be successful? No
4: Will everyone who studies at Azad University not be successful? No
5: Is there a difference between state and Azad students in the job market? Yes
6: Was I satisfied with Azad University? Very much yes
7: When I came to the state university, was my knowledge less than the students here? No
8: Are the professors at state universities better than Azad University? Yes
9: Were job opportunities and forming effective work connections more at the state university than Azad? Yes
10: Did the state university cause more growth for me? Yes

blocks.text: The Three Main Differences
Maybe I can summarize the most important differences between state and Azad universities in three words:
My Bachelor's at Azad: Drama and Fun

When I started my bachelor's at Azad University, I found very very good friends. I was an 18-year-old kid who had only heard that you shouldn't fall in love in the first term. Didn't I? No, I fell in love in term 3 😂
I really managed to find very good friends at Azad University. Very good people, full of drama, full of challenges, and full of strange stories that I really don't want to go into detail about here.

I have a ton of good memories from Azad University and that's only because of the really cool kids who studied there. Of course, in my opinion, hearing other people's dramas and being in cool crews means being cool...
Was there any studying? No.

There, maybe less than 1% of people were there for studying. Most were after fun, parties, crews, and passing time. Which was exactly the opposite in my experience at state universities. Here they also chase drama and strange stories, but the percentage is much lower than at Azad.
So: if you really like to have fun and enjoy your student years, Azad University is the best choice you can have.
The Academic Reality at Azad
But! What about academically?
The reality is that the students there were really weak. When I compare what the bachelor's students at the University of Isfahan do with them, I really realize that 90% were really dumbasses.
The issue is that they really don't get anything and just get a degree and then go work in unrelated jobs. That's it!
So if you're looking for a university where the studying vibe and academically active students matter to you, Azad is exactly the place that will disappoint you.
So what about me? I was an exception :) It's the truth, well.
I had my own crew, I had good friendships, but I always kept myself in the studying and education phase and such.
Yeah man, I had drama too.
Also, let me add that 95% of the boys and girls there were really assholes. Really assholes. Really...
State University: Better Academics, More Pressure
State universities also have assholes 😂 Our incoming class, most are really assholes.
State university creates a very pretentious atmosphere. Where the person's pride is that they study at a state university. That's how stupid it is.

But really in terms of being active, professors, doing research and publishing papers, having research labs, students being active, and so on, state university is 100 times better than Azad. It's really not comparable.
The connections and scientific and research experiences you can have at a state university, 1% of that isn't at Azad.
But there's also a lot more pressure and you really have to work hard.
I understood the real meaning of a supervisor at a state university. I learned the real meaning of trying hard and exams that were actually exams at a state university.
I made very meaningful connections that led to money.
Was it worth all that time? For me personally, yes.
Maybe for someone else the answer is no.
Azad's Advantage: Less Pressure, More Freedom

Another good thing about Azad University was that the pressure of university and studying was less, and if the student themselves followed up, they could learn a lot of skills and work a lot at the same time. But at a state university this is less. I'm not saying it's not there at all, but it's less.
But maybe it's interesting for you to know, when I talk to my current friends they all agree on this point:
In my opinion, getting a computer bachelor's at a state university is not worth it.

The bachelor's courses aren't that related to software and AI and such, and really at a state university they are very strict about these things which in my opinion really isn't worth it in practice :)
But for higher degrees, Azad University really has nothing to say compared to state.

For me personally, coming to a state university was a very very very correct choice and I will be satisfied with this choice for the rest of my life :) both financially and in terms of research, science, and credibility.
Really everything I know and am an expert in is because of this choice and I'm very satisfied with it.
The Job Market and Degree Bias

By the way, let me also say this point that for working, there are some places that care about the degree and sometimes I've seen they differentiate between Azad and state university students. In my opinion it's not right of course... but well such a thing exists in the job market.
Final Thoughts: No Real Credibility
In the end, all state and Azad universities in Iran have no particular credibility in the world. Even Sharif and Tehran and...
Yes, you read that right, they have no particular credibility.

Studying at a particular university in Iran and in this messed up situation is not a particular achievement. Maybe universities have become a safe place for students to have less stress about entering the job market and escape from the reality of life more.
I don't know...
But in my opinion the academic future in Iran is black :)
So whether you want to study at Sharif, or study at Azad...
